cohort: The study included 26,211 births and their mothers in Estonia from 2020 and 2021.
finding: SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy was associated with an increased risk of stillbirth and perinatal mortality, but not with Apgar score, cesarean section, preeclampsia, or preterm birth; vaccination slightly decreased the impact on perinatal mortality.
mod_finding: SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy was not associated with a higher risk of cesarean section.
